summary: Proposes experimental TLS extensions that use opaque pinning tickets to pin a server's identity. In the first session the server gives the client an encrypted ticket, and on later connections the server proves it still holds the matching secret, which helps spot a wrongly issued certificate.

eli5.summary: The first time you meet, the server hands you a secret token. Next time, only the real server can show it knows what the token means, so impostors are caught.

questions: how to pin tls server identity
